claims.value: Toreno gives side A 3,000 cavalry with Kellermann’s assembled approach force at Carpio on 25 November, not a whole-field Alba total.
claims.rationale: Approach population, not automatically carried forward intact to Alba. English rendering (ours): "Kellermann, gathering all the force he could, including three thousand cavalry, appeared before Carpio on the 25th."

citations.locator: toreno-t3, printed p. 165, Internet Archive leaf 170; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: el general Kellermann reuniendo toda la fuerza que pudo, entre ella 3000 caballos, se mostró el 25 delante del Carpió.

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 800 cavalry beside Losada’s first division on the right, not the entire Spanish army.
claims.rationale: Sector subset; no infantry number or full local total inferred. English rendering (ours): "Our right, where Losada’s first division and eight hundred cavalry were situated."

citations.locator: toreno-t3, printed p. 166, Internet Archive leaf 171; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: nuestra derecha, en donde se hallaba la primera división del mando de Losada y 800 caballos.

claims.value: Jourdan describes Kellermann choosing to attack while infantry and artillery were still distant.
claims.rationale: Subsequent Lorcet/Millet cavalry tasks are subordinate; no all-arms opening assumption. English rendering (ours): "Although his infantry and artillery were still distant, he did not hesitate to begin the attack."

claims.value: Jourdan describes Kellermann’s opening attack before the infantry arrived.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Although his infantry and artillery were still distant, he began the attack."

claims.value: Toreno places Mendizabal at the head of the left-wing vanguard and second-division subset, distinct from del Parque’s overall command.
claims.rationale: An attributed local command observation; not automatic credit for all named officers. English rendering (ours): "The left wing, Carrera’s vanguard and part of the second division, held firm with Mendizabal at its head."

claims.value: Toreno describes Alba on the right bank with a stone bridge to the opposite bank.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "The town on the right bank of the Tormes communicates with the opposite bank by a stone bridge."

claims.value: Jourdan and Toreno place the encounter on 28 November, conflicting with the frozen Bodart date of 26 November.
claims.rationale: Calendar disagreement retained; frozen entry unchanged. Not a claim that morning entry and afternoon attack are simultaneous. English rendering (ours): "He found the Spanish army in position on the 28th around three in the afternoon; [Toreno] our men entered Alba on the morning of the 28th."
